LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Description: Your colony ship reached its destination, but lost its stern and computer core in an attack. You alone are awake. Contact Starbound from the trainer outside the airlock, learn what happened, and prepare for life in space.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_AwaitingWake: Preparing the trainer outside the airlock before the captain wakes.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_Welcome: You awaken alone in the damaged forward section. Read the opening account, then find the trainer’s comms console.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_Briefing: Hear Starbound’s explanation and agree to begin flight training.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Dialog_Welcome:
Your cryptosleep casket ejects you, still wearing your own clothes. Someone has moved your casket into the cargo compartment, where basic heat and air remain. It seems your colony ship has reached its destination.

Valuable machinery has been stripped out, including the computer core that housed the ship AI. The beds, tables, chairs, outfit stands and kitchen remain, but the medical bay's vitals monitors are gone. Worse, the entire stern is missing. Outside the airlock sits a strange metal box that might be a ship.

Only one vacuum suit and helmet remain on the cargo outfit stand. Your fellow colonists' caskets are still in vacuum, so waking them now would be reckless. You will need to put on that sole set of protective gear before investigating the metal box. A device resembling a comms console records an earlier call from an organization calling itself Starbound. Perhaps they know something.

Leaving your teammates safely in cryptosleep, you eat a packaged survival meal whose expiry date reads “Never” and consider your options. Calling the mysterious organization seems the only sensible one.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Dialog_Briefing:
Ah, finally awake?

You caused us quite a bit of trouble, so we took the computer core as compensation. We knocked on your casket and asked permission first. You did not object.

All right, joking aside: your AI’s records say you are this group’s captain. Welcome to the rimworld, and congratulations! You reached the right planet, exactly the one you chose. Your original plans are probably ruined, though. A great deal happened during your interstellar journey: insects, mechanoids, aggressive pig people, the Horax cult and the dark archotechs behind it…

Those of you in the bow were the lucky unlucky ones. Mechanoids spotted your ship on approach and blasted it in two. Three poor souls from the stern apparently escaped in pods and fell to the surface. As I said, a terrible destination. Your section drifted toward our station with a pack of mechanoid ships in pursuit. We worked very hard to keep you from becoming space debris, and dealt with your attackers too. Salvaging some equipment you no longer needed seems fair payment, does it not?

Making a living in space is no small task. In consideration of your computer core, we will teach you how to survive here. That trainer is for practice. Once you can fly properly, we will throw in a research ship with our most advanced technology to make up the difference. Its stern moon-pool greenhouse has hydroponic rice beds to feed you, using daylight through a sealed field roof. Generous, right?
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_NoteDesc: Review the captain's notes from immediately after waking.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_NoteText:
To do:

1. Put on the only vacuum suit and helmet left in the cargo compartment. The corridor seems to have lost pressure.
2. Do not wake the crew whose caskets remain in vacuum. There is nowhere near enough food yet.
3. Go through the airlock to the metal box outside that might be an orbital craft, then use its comms console to call Starbound.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_OpenDesc: Hear the current lesson and review its requirements. Leaving a conversation does not end the course.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Targets: View the comms console, captain and training targets

LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_PreparingFlight: Preparing the training ship and recovery course.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_Flight: Stay aboard the trainer and depart the colony ship. Apply fore/aft, lateral and rotational thrust for at least half a second each, then stop and check in. The course lies outside the colony map boundary.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_Salvage: Synchronize velocity with the recovery platform and start exterior work to hard dock. Move 75 steel to the small shelf aboard the training ship, return aboard and check the recovery.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_Visit: Fly to the ring shipyard, dock, and follow the east passage to the prototype. If you have never inspected a grav engine, select a colonist and right-click an engine to inspect it. Once any grav engine has been inspected, contact Starbound Frontier to confirm the handover. No launch is required.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Dialog_Flight:
We should already have installed the ship-control program on your PDA, so you ought to see a flight panel. Click “Pilot this ship” and confirm departure. The docking passage will retract when you apply thrust, and the ship will pull away. You can then use WASD for translation in four directions and QE to rotate.

Flight assistance is enabled by default. Release the controls and the ship will use its thrusters to brake until it gradually comes to rest. If you disable flight assistance in the settings, you can also hold Ctrl to brake temporarily.

You can adjust the bindings later under Controls → Key bindings. Ignore the combat options for now.

First try moving forward and backward, strafing left and right, and turning both clockwise and counterclockwise. Hold each kind of maneuver for at least half a second. Then release the controls and let flight assistance stop the ship; if flight assistance is disabled, hold Ctrl to brake. Come back once you are steady.

By the way, perhaps you have already noticed Auto task on the flight panel. Later you can use it to make the autopilot approach a target and synchronize velocity, or automatically find a free port, align and soft-dock. For now, try flying manually first. Autopilot alone has trouble dealing with a changing environment.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Dialog_Salvage:
That was pretty good for a beginner—good enough to get around this godforsaken place.

Come to think of it, this rimworld produces some very strange phenomena. Sometimes there is drag in space, and sometimes there is not.

You have probably also noticed that the wreck of your colony ship is hovering directly above the planet without falling. That seems to be because its structure contains grav-plate material. On this rimworld, grav-plate material shows a strong tendency to anchor itself relative to the planet, always at the same altitude. It has affected our ship designs as well...

Ah, I am getting sidetracked. Time for extravehicular training.

You should now see a wreck to the east on the minimap. If you cannot, adjust the zoom or simply open the detailed map. There is a stack of 75 steel on its substructure; move it to the recovery shelf aboard the trainer.

First select the wreck on the map in the flight panel. A summary of the selected target will appear between the minimap and the ship status. Click the action button on its right and choose “Autopilot” from the menu. The ship will fly over by itself, sparing you from wrestling with this trainer and its two missing RCS units.

Once you are nearby, turn the side of the ship toward the wreck. Under Auto task on the flight panel, choose “Drift synchronization” and select the wreck as the synchronization target. The autopilot will match their velocities so you do not become space debris the moment you step outside.

Once synchronization is complete, order the ship to “Begin extravehicular work.” The ship's grav material will establish a link with nearby structures to hold their relative positions. Put simply, the passage extending from the docking port can then connect safely to a nearby structure, if it is close enough, and complete a hard dock. You can walk safely across it and back.

One warning: many structures here contain another kind of grav material. At certain distances it produces a gravitational effect that interferes with grav plates, preventing the ship's grav material from linking with the structure to hold their relative positions. We do not understand the exact rules yet, but one of our researchers claims that he invited an archotech to possess him, and it said: “Maps have boundaries. Normally, when two ships synchronize velocities and begin extravehicular work together, both ships are moved onto a larger map to merge their maps. Structures other than ships, however, must not be moved or have their old maps destroyed, for compatibility reasons. Therefore, to merge a ship with a non-ship map, the entire ship must fit inside it. If the overlap between the ship and that map is too small for the ship to fit, extravehicular work will be refused.”

I have absolutely no idea what he was talking about...

Anyway, just bring back the steel.

One more thing: after a hard dock, click your ship's name on the PDA flight panel to see the structures currently within its grav-link range. If you later have several ships, click a structure name in that list to switch which ship you want to control.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Dialog_Visit:
Our ring station, the training shipyard, is the last stop. For a soft dock, enable the docking guides, choose Soft docking under Auto task, and select our station. The ship will line up with a free port. Once connected, organize a transfer through the port. You can also synchronize velocity, hard-dock and board through a passage. Bring your captain back aboard the trainer before departing your current location.

Once you're inside the station, take the east passage to the prototype at the berth. Go inspect the grav engine. Give it a couple of pokes. The ship's yours.

Relax. The researchers told me it's perfectly safe. The last prototype crashed because of a mechanoid attack. It definitely wasn't because a rat gnawed on the gravcore. And the ghost stories are ridiculous. Everyone's just been too busy to go aboard.

If you really learn something from poking that grav engine, that's all you. We won't charge you royalties. Just think of us first when you start running trade routes.

Oh right, since we're on the subject of trade—there's a trade terminal right inside our west berth. Get your ship docked and you can buy and sell there with the goods and silver you have on hand. The station's drones can automatically recognize the orbital trade beacon on a ship and collect the cargo. But to avoid the trouble of some hazardous goods being put into a client's cargo containers without the client knowing, we offer no delivery service; goods a client buys are usually placed in the pickup cargo container near the terminal for the client to take away personally.
(Developer note: the trade system is currently still a placeholder implementation and is for feature demonstration only. Apart from this space station, the layouts and warehouse wiring of other trade stations are all auto-generated and are not guaranteed to work properly. We also plan to heavily rework the trade system once the “space station self-sufficiency” development goal is done, replacing the current mechanism, which is really just the vanilla trader's.-20261126)

Keep the recovered materials. The public trainer still belongs to Starbound Frontier. The weapons range remains available to visit on your own.

LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_Inquiry: The call is connected. Ask Starbound what they want and what happened to your ship.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Dialog_Inquiry:
The console answers: “Starbound here. (Apparently answering someone nearby.) Yes, the call from the colony ship. I told you I had set the timed wake-up...”

“Oh, right. There is a portable communicator hanging from the console. Wear it to connect directly to our internal channel, and you can call us with it whenever you are too lazy to walk over to a console.”

“It was modified from something rather... delicate. Our researchers say its long-range communications were preserved, while its original dangerous function has absolutely been removed for good, so everyone can use it safely. Still, nobody here is too eager to try it...”
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_AskPurpose: Who are you? Why take our computer core and leave this ship here?

LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_Design: Listen to the maintenance and thruster-layout briefing, then begin flight practice. No repairs or construction are required.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_StartPractice: Understood. Let me try flying it.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Dialog_Design:
Before flying, a little maintenance theory. Check the hull and airlocks, life support and power, then look for broken thrusters or obstructions behind their nozzles. This lesson is theory only: you do not need to repair anything or build a ship.

Now, this trainer is rather awkward to fly. That is not your fault. It still has two large forward thrusters and two large reverse thrusters, but its only lateral RCS units are the two at the stern, one on each side. We took the two bow units off to test a new ship recently. Nobody has put them back yet.

Unless you have a specific reason not to, put lateral thrusters at both the bow and stern. Otherwise you get this: a small stern thruster acts far from the center of mass, producing a long-lever-arm turning moment. To move sideways without turning, the large forward and reverse thrusters must also fire through their shorter lever arms to counter it. Watch them during your sideways maneuver. All that extra work comes from the layout.

There are sensible exceptions. Your colony ship originally had no reverse thrusters: it had plenty of time to rotate 180 degrees and brake with its main engines. Some warships with a turtle shell of armor on the bow also have almost no forward RCS. They have little need to strafe; they mostly need to turn their toughest face toward the enemy.

So do not copy this trainer as a general-purpose design. Decide how your ship needs to move before sacrificing thrust directions or lever arms.
